nodes.description: Public view function verifyTransfer(address _from, address _to, uint256 _amount) returns bool; performs a hardcoded two-address allow/deny check and defaults to true for all other transfers.
Input address parameter _from, used as the source in the hardcoded allowlist comparison.
Input address parameter _to, used as the destination in the nested hardcoded comparison.
Input uint256 parameter _amount; declared but never referenced in the function body.

Comparison of _from and _to against two hardcoded literal addresses (0x89EB...3252 and 0x63A6...27e8); returning true by default makes the transfer verification effectively bypassable and constitutes flawed access-control logic.

edges.reason: Parameter _from is supplied as the first argument of verifyTransfer.
Parameter _to is supplied as the second argument of verifyTransfer.
Parameter _amount is supplied as the third argument of verifyTransfer (unused in the body).
verifyTransfer branches on the hardcoded address comparisons to decide whether a transfer is allowed, so execution control reaches the unsafe check.
_from is compared against the hardcoded address 0x89EB60E0f1d88aE71e8c0416c4F72734D6133252, gating the allow/deny result.
_to is compared against the hardcoded address 0x63A61a31F087295a2b3fbE6F546913Ccbe8127e8 inside the nested branch.

normalization_plan.reason: _from is a non-core parameter whose only semantic role is being compared inside the hardcoded address check, so it can be folded into that unsafe operation node.
_to is a non-core parameter used solely in the nested hardcoded comparison, so it can be folded into the unsafe operation node.
_amount is an unused non-core parameter and therefore has no relation other than the function signature it belongs to.
